obligations.note: The new 'payment-advice' integration uses https://advice.fernbrook.example/v1, satisfying the TLS requirement. The exhaustive control test test_integrations_use_tls passed in CI.

The new asset-inventory entry for 'payment-advice' has an empty owner field ("owner": ""). The obligation requires every integration to be listed with an owner and a data classification. The exhaustive control test test_integrations_are_inventoried failed with 'no owner', and test_inventory_entries_have_owner_and_classification also failed.
Ticket CHG-25317 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt, and its components (payments.integrations, payments.controls-data) cover both files modified by this change.
Mara Costa (change_approver, payments-eng, not the author Jonah Weiss) provided a code_review approval on the head commit, satisfying the independent-approval requirement.
There is only one commit in the change; the approval references that same commit 8414e2b, so it covers exactly what is merged.

The CI run on the final commit 8414e2b shows result 'failure' with 2 failing tests (test_integrations_are_inventoried and test_inventory_entries_have_owner_and_classification). The full suite is not passing, so the testing requirement is not met.

The change touches integrations.py (component payments.integrations, security_sensitive=true). A security_review approval from Ines Halvorsen (security_reviewer, platform-security) on the correct commit is present.

The change modifies controls/payments/asset-inventory.json (a protected path). A control_owner approval from Bao Tran (controls-office, not the author's payments-eng team) on the correct commit is present.

summary: The change adds a new 'payment-advice' outbound integration to payments and registers it in the asset inventory, but the inventory entry has an empty owner field, violating INV-1 (every integration must have an owner and data classification). This is confirmed by two failing control tests in CI: test_integrations_are_inventoried and test_inventory_entries_have_owner_and_classification. Because the CI run on the final commit does not show the full suite passing, CHG-4 is also refuted. The change cannot be accepted until the owner is populated and the control tests pass.
